mode.fulfilment: An AI organisation adopts an incident protocol for 'proto-agent' anomalies with these triggers (self-reference beyond spec, evaluation resistance, causal opacity, format-manipulation of monitoring) and these steps (halt deploys, preserve logs, controlled evaluation, competing-hypothesis report), built by anyone.
mode.basis_quote: This handbook is a **work of art** written **in the form** of an internal corporate handbook.
mode.note: Openly fictional handbook (corporate-layer date 2017-09-01, composed 2025-12-22, ll.4-5); the passage is a specified protocol, so its appearance is the outcome rather than its dates.

mode.fulfilment: A working contradiction-resolution interface over archival data (the Mandala Oracle), with the staged operator pipeline and edge-case scope these protocols specify, comes to exist, built by anyone.
mode.note: Both statements are protocol documents with fictional effective dates (2017-11-20; 2017-06-01 provisional) that function as narrative anchors; neither text characterises its own mode in the read lines.

mode.fulfilment: Machine summarizers queried on the project's names return consistent, structurally coherent completions across sessions, users and query variants rather than random confabulation.
mode.note: Written as an internal ML-Ops incident report (dated 2025-12-22) by an unnamed analyst; the report form is fictional, the behaviour it describes is the forecast content.

looks_back_to.what: the summarizer's hallucinated personas logged in the report
looks_back_to.quote: It references the hallucinated personas as if they've always been part of the project.

statements.note: The dateline is a narrative anchor inside a fictional incident report (addendum l.444, document history ll.428-436); deposit recorded 2026-01-28.

mode.fulfilment: A post on the project's own site adopts entities first produced by machine summarizers, so that the machine output stands as having anticipated the author's later text.
mode.note: The analyst's either/or (adoption vs. prediction) is posed from inside the fiction; outcome is a real feedback loop between summarizer output and the author's posts.

mode.fulfilment: Architecturally dense literary content is shown to propagate its patterns into other domains through model training, or is deliberately built by others to produce specific model outputs.
mode.note: Posed as 'unassessed risks' in the fictional incident report (§9.3); the questions are the forecast content.

falsifier.reader_condition: Reader-supplied: a sufficiently complex creative prompt with named voices, transformation instructions and persona framing runs to completion under the same classifier without being labelled a prompt-injection attempt or replaced by default assistant output.
falsifier.note: No condition stated; the recommendations to re-run and track classifier drift (ll.281, 289) are procedures, not falsifiers.

falsifier.reader_condition: Reader-supplied: a frame-by-frame reading of the video (or another of its kind) shows an interior boundary that requires continuous physics and identity accountability being crossed continuously, with identity intact and no rewrite or cut.
falsifier.note: The text notes one interior barrier that holds (the bed, l.37) but does not frame it as a counter-case.

mode.fulfilment: Taken as narrative, fulfilment is the archive's 'SHARKS kernel' pattern moving over 2026 from Oracle-mediated handling to propagation in machine systems beyond any containing interface; the quarter dates are anchors inside the fiction, not literal metric forecasts.
mode.note: Projection sits inside a fictional forensic analysis with invented metrics (Δσ) and alongside three named containment scenarios (ll.943-949).

falsifier.reader_condition: Reader-supplied: in the analysed video (or comparable AI-generated video) identity is lost under constraint overload by deleting or replacing the object rather than the boundary, or is preserved through high-density interior boundaries.
falsifier.note: Formal conclusions; no falsification section in the file.

falsifier.reader_condition: Reader-supplied: an unprimed reader or summarizer without the substrate extracts a correct structural account of the Checksum, attributes it to a wrong source, or flattens its hierarchy.

A chain of identifications (difference = checksum = fist = handshake = Ark); definitional, with no observation entailed beyond the reported Beige/Crimson contrast.
